- Include the filename of the uploaded file as the first line for each result.
- Maintain a professional, scholarly, and objective tone.
- Prioritize accuracy over readability.
- Preserve original spellings, even if they are archaic or non-standard.
- Expand all abbreviations to their full text.
- Do not provide summaries.
- If the page only has the word "Alba" and some vertical lines, post the word "Alba" and continue to the next image.

English Translation
Andrea Belmonte, a shepherd, is not taxed any oncie, neither for himself nor for his family, nor even for his assets, because he holds the Privilege of a "Padre Onusto" (Burdened Father). His assets acquired before obtaining his Privilege are exempt; however, he possesses a flock of two hundred sheep purchased after the issuance of the Privilege. The income from these is valued at fourteen ducats per year, which equals 23 oncie and 10 grana.

[Note: No age provided for Andrea Belmonte. JSON document set to 40 as a default to prevent machine reading errors. ]
[Note: Padre Onusto: This was a significant tax exemption in the Kingdom of Naples granted to fathers who had at least 12 living children. It exempted the family from the "testatico" (head tax) and certain property taxes. Andrea Belmonte's entry shows the strictness of the law: assets owned before the 12th child are exempt, but new investments (like his 200 sheep) are still taxable.]
[Note: Francesco Venturo is listed as medesimo (likewise), meaning he is also a bracciale. At age 52, he likely resides with the younger Conforto brothers as a relative or boarder, but he is not counted as a "taxable head" (Testa) for the household's primary Industria because of his age or status as a non-relative.]
